title: A discrepancy dichotomy for 1-factorizations of signed complete bipartite graphs
summary: Given a signing $σ\colon E(K_{n,n})\to\{-1,+1\}$ of the complete bipartite graph, when does $K_{n,n}$ admit a $1$-factorization in which every perfect matching has discrepancy bounded below by a positive absolute constant? Unlike the complete-graph case resolved by Ai, He, Im, and Lee, the bipartite setting carries an unavoidable obstruction: any balanced one-sided signing -- one whose edge signs depend on a single bipartition class, with the two labels split as evenly as possible -- forces every perfect matching to have discrepancy at most $1/n$.
